Motiur Rahman Mithu

full_judgment:
8. After conclusion of taking evidence, the appellant was examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which he pleaded not guilty and refused to adduce any evidence for his defence. After conclusion of the trial, learned Tribunal Judge of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Moulavibazar, by his the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 26.09.2006 convicted the appellant as aforesaid. 

 10. Mr. Shaheen Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, after taking us through the entire evidence on record submits that in passing the impugned judgment and order the learned Tribunal Judge, seriously failed to consider that the prosecution totally failed to prove their case by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence. The learned Tribunal Judge, also failed to consider the defence case, which more probable that the appellant was falsely implicated in the instant case. He further submits that the complainant filed this complaint-petition against the appellant, at the instigation of one Monnaf Member and all of the prosecution witnesses are partisaned and interested witnesses and they failed to corroborate each other on material points. He also submits that there is no eye witness of the alleged occurrences but the learned Tribunal Judge, relying upon interested witnesses convicted the appellant. They are no independent and disinterested witnesses in this case to prove the prosecution case and there is no explanation from the side of the prosecution as to why their non-production of any witnesses from surrounding area, as if, they would have been examined, will not support the prosecution case. As such, the convict-appellant is entitled to get benefit of doubt under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. 

 11. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellant is not any way involved with the said incident of rape rather he has been falsely implicated in this case. He also submits that the alleged incident took place on 28.03.2002 and the complaint was filed on 21.10,2003, after a long delay which cast serious doubt as to the truthfulness of the prosecution case. He next submits that on 09.10.2002 the victim filed a complaint petition, wherein she alleged that she was raped by one Khalilur Rahman master and after one year later she claimed that she was not raped by the Khalilur Rahman but by the appellant Motiur Rahman and filed this instant case, at this stage, it is difficult to ascertain, which version of the complainant's allegation is true. He also submits that the victim was not medically examination to ascertain the same. He further submits that the Tribunal failed to appreciate the evidence on record and came to a wrong finding and erroneous decision, thereby convicted and sentenced of the appellant, which is not sustainable in law. He lastly submits that the prosecution failed to prove their case by producing any independent, disinterested witnesses from neighbouring area, as such; convicting the appellant relying on depositions of these interested witnesses is unsafe and liable to be set aside. 

 13. Mr. Bhishmadev Chakrabortty, the learned Deputy-Attorney General appearing for the state submits that that all facts have been proved by the cogent, credible and reliable evidence of the prosecution witnesses. He also submits that the learned Judge, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal rightly found the appellant guilty under Sections 9(1)/13(a)(c) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. So, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence do not call for airy interference from this court. He further submits that the learned Judge, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal was perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the appellant on the basis of cogent and reliable evidence and his judgment does not suffer from any misreading and non-reading of evidence. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that all the prosecution witnesses are natural, probable and competent witnesses. He further submits that the prosecution proved their case beyond reasonable doubt. There is no contradiction in their statements on any material point. The teamed Judge rightly and correctly put reliance on the testimony of the P.Ws. 1, 2, 8 and 9 and convicted and sentenced the appellant as aforesaid. There is no illegality or irregularity in the said judgment and order of conviction and sentence, the prosecution witnesses corroborated with each other on material points and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be upheld by this Court. He further submits that if the appellant give consent to D.N.A. test to ascertain the paternity of the child to resolve any dispute whatsoever, the state has no object to it. He lastly submits that the allegations against the appellant under section 9(1) read with section 13 (a) (c) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 has been well proved by the prosecution and as such, the appeal preferred by the appellant should be dismissed. 

 14. To appreciate the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment, it is necessary to scrutinize the law and evidence relating to the facts of the case. Before going to the merit of the case we have to scrutinize the evidence of prosecution witnesses. 

 17. We have gone through the Petition of Complaint, Inquiry Report, deposition of the witnesses, impugned judgment and order grounds taken in the petition of appeal and other materials on record and given our anxious consideration to the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for both the sides. We find that the appellant was convicted and sentenced on the basis of the evidence adduced by the victim P.W.-1, Rahima Begum P.W.-2, Bacchu Miah P.W. 8 Md. Kana Miah, and P.W-9, Maya Beg and circumstantial evidence. 

 18. First question raised by teamed Advocate for the convict-appellant that whether or not all the prosecution witnesses are interested witnesses, the complainant at the instigation of Monnaf Member filed this complaint-petition against the appellant and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court against the convict-appellant on the basis of the evidence of interested, inter-related and partisan witnesses is sustainable in law. The evidence of interested, inter-related and partisan witnesses must be closely scrutinized before it is accepted. We find support of this contention in the case of Nawabul Alam and ors. Vs. The State, 15 BLD (AD)) page 61, wherein it is held: 

 "The principle that is to be followed is that the evidence of persons falling in the category of interested, interrelated and partisan witnesses, must be closely and critically scrutinized They should not be accepted on their face value. Their evidence cannot be rejected outright simply because they are interested witnesses for that will result in a failure of justice, but their evidence is liable to be scrutinized with more care and caution than is necessary in the case of disinterested and unrelated witnesses. An interested witness is one who has a motive for falsely implication an accused person and that is the reason why his evidence is initially suspected. His evidence has to cross the hurdle of critical appreciation. As his evidence cannot be thrown out mechanically because of his interestedness, so his evidence cannot be accepted mechanically without a critical examination." 

 21. Last question is whether or not the learned Judge of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Moulvibazar is justified in convicting and sentencing the appellant Motiur Rahman Mithu under sections 9(1)/13(a)(c) of the Narj-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. In the instant case, we find that the victim Complainant P.W.-1, Rahima Begum used to stay at the residence of one Khalil master as a maid servant. The convict-appellant Matiur Rahman Mithu, the brother-in-law of Khalil Master also stayed at that house. Having been staying there he used to continue his student life indeed. The convict-appellant's brother-in-law Khalil Master and his sister Parul Begum are primary school teachers. They used to go their respectively schools by keeping their minor son, victim Rahima and the convict Mithu at their house. On the fateful date of occurrence i.e. on 140 Choitra, two years back, corresponding to 28.03.2002, at about 12.00-12.30 p.m. taking undue advantage and opportunity of her loneliness the convict-appellant Matiur Rahman Mithu forcibly outraged her chastity and modesty against her will. Later on the appellant has continued his lust for her and raped the victim repeatedly on several occasions by expressing the assurance of marrying her. Consequently, the victim-complainant has conceived. The victim's father came to see her, after six month of the said incident, at that time; the victim informed the above incident stating all the factual matters and affairs to her father as well as Khalil master and his wife Parul Begum. Subsequently, she came back to their house with her father. Chairman Mobisshar Ali, father of convict-appellant gave an amount of Taka 23,000 to the victim's father to abort her pregnancy. Henceforth, she gave birth to a son namely Ibrahim in the due course of time. The father of the victim namely Royab Ullah, at the instigation of Chairman Mobasshir Ali, filed a criminal case on false and fabricated allegations against Khalil Master by fraudulently obtaining her L.T.I. In fact, the convict-appellant Matiur Rahman Mithu is the real culprit for her unsolicited pregnancy and for becoming a maiden mother. P.W.-2 Bacchu Miah, in his testimony testified that he heard from the victim Rahima Begum that the sole accused Matiur Rahman Mithu has violated her modesty and virginity. Admittedly, P.W. 3 Fatik Miah, P.W. 4 Naior Mirth, P.W. 5 Khurshed Ahmed, P.W. 6 Toiyab Ali and the P.W. 7 Md. Badsha Miah were tendered by the prosecution and defence declined to cross examine them. P.W-8, Kana Miah, in his deposition deposed that the victim-complainant Rahima Begum came to his house and informed him that the accused Matiur Rahman has raped her. As a result, she became pregnant. P.W.-9 Md. Maya Beg, in his testimony, testified that the victim Rahima came to his house and informed him that the accused Matiur Rahman has raped her on several occasions and for that reason she has conceived. The aforesaid averments, contentions and deliberations of the prosecution witnesses, it is observed that the victim complainant Rahima Begum has elaborately asserted and contended her complaint petition and deposed all the factual matters and affairs from the beginning to the ends in her examination-in-chief. Afterwards, she has very strongly and vehemently defended herself in her cross-examination. Other Prosecution witnesses namely P.W.-2 Bacchu Miah, P.W-8, Kana Miah and P.W.-9 Md. Maya Beg supported the prosecution case. The allegations against the appellant under section 9(1) read with section 13 (a) (c) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 has been well proved by the prosecution as the chain of circumstantial evidence connects the convict appellant in raping of the victim Rahima Begum, due to this illegal forceful inter-course, she became pregnant and delivered a son namely Ibrahim in the due course of time and thereby appellant have committed offence under Sections 90 (1)13(a)(c) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. As there is no break in the chain of causation and chain or circumstances connecting the appellant with the raping of the victim Rahima Begum and as circumstantial evidence is more cogent than the evidence of eye witness, the learned Tribunal Judge after perusing the materials on record rightly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
